qas.q: What does InspectCar's used car inspection check?
qas.a: InspectCar's 300+ point inspection covers: Exterior body panels and paint (including paint gauge test), engine and transmission performance, OBD diagnostic scan for fault codes, interior condition and all electrical systems, tyre condition and tread depth, underbody inspection for rust and leaks, suspension and steering, AC performance, and document verification including RC, insurance, and PUC.

qas.q: Does InspectCar check the engine of a used car?
qas.a: Yes. The engine check includes: visual inspection of the engine bay for leaks, oil condition check, coolant level and condition, cold start test for abnormal smoke or noise, idle RPM check, transmission fluid check, and a full OBD scan reading all engine-related fault codes and live sensor data.

qas.q: What is a paint gauge test and what does it reveal?
qas.a: A paint thickness gauge uses an electromagnetic sensor to measure the paint coat depth on each body panel in microns. Original factory paint is 90–130 microns thick. A panel that has been repainted after accident repair shows 160–300+ microns. This test reveals hidden accident history that looks perfectly normal to the naked eye — it is one of the most important tools in a used car inspection.

qas.q: Does InspectCar check tyres during inspection?
qas.a: Yes. Tyre inspection includes: tread depth measurement on all 4 tyres, check for uneven wear patterns (indicating alignment or suspension problems), sidewall damage, tyre age verification using the DOT manufacturing code (tyres over 5 years old should be replaced regardless of tread), spare tyre condition, and wheel rim condition.

qas.q: Does InspectCar inspect the underbody?
qas.a: Yes. The underbody inspection checks for: chassis rust or structural corrosion, evidence of major repairs or welding (indicating accident frame damage), fluid leaks from the engine, gearbox, or differential, exhaust system condition, suspension arm and bush condition, and any impact damage from driving over large obstacles.

qas.q: What electrical systems are tested in the inspection?
qas.a: All electrical systems are tested including: battery health (CCA testing), alternator output, all exterior lights (headlights, tail lights, indicators, DRLs, fog lights), interior lights, AC compressor and blower, all power windows, central locking, horn, reverse camera or sensors, USB ports, infotainment system, and any OBD-reported electrical fault codes.

qas.q: Does InspectCar verify documents during inspection?
qas.a: Yes. Document verification includes: checking that the RC book matches the vehicle's chassis number and engine number, verifying insurance validity, checking PUC certificate validity, checking for hypothecation endorsement (active loan), verifying the odometer reading against the service book entries, and confirming the vehicle is not under any court order or blacklisted.

qas.q: Can car inspection detect accident damage in a used car?
qas.a: Yes. Accident damage is detected through: paint thickness gauge readings (repainted panels), panel gap measurements (misaligned body panels after repair), OBD fault codes related to airbag or ABS systems, visual inspection of the firewall and chassis for repair welds, and underbody inspection for bent or repaired structural members.

qas.q: Can InspectCar detect odometer tampering?
qas.a: Yes. Odometer tampering is detected by cross-referencing the displayed reading with: physical wear indicators (accelerator pedal rubber, driver seat fabric, steering wheel wear), service book stamp dates and km entries, OBD ECU total odometer memory (in some vehicles), and tyre age vs claimed mileage.

qas.q: How do I know if a used car has been in a flood?
qas.a: Flood damage indicators include: musty or moldy smell inside the cabin, waterline marks visible under the seats or in the boot, corrosion on fuse box terminals and connectors, mud residue in the spare tyre well or under the carpet, sticky or seized door hinges, condensation inside headlamps, and corroded or replaced electrical connectors.

qas.q: Can car inspection find if the car has an unpaid loan?
qas.a: InspectCar verifies the RC book for hypothecation (loan) endorsement. If a lender (bank/NBFC) is listed on the RC, the vehicle has an active loan. The seller cannot legally transfer ownership without an NOC from the lender. We advise buyers to demand Form 35 (NOC) and check the Parivahan portal for this verification.

qas.q: What if the seller refuses to allow a car inspection?
qas.a: A seller refusing an independent inspection is a major red flag. Legitimate sellers with nothing to hide welcome inspections. InspectCar recommends walking away from any deal where the seller refuses to allow an independent third-party inspection.

qas.q: Can inspection reveal if a car has been modified illegally?
qas.a: Yes. Our inspectors check for modifications that may affect roadworthiness, safety, or insurance validity, including non-standard suspension, modified engine components, illegal LPG/CNG kit installations, and aftermarket electrical modifications. Such modifications can void insurance claims.

qas.q: Can InspectCar check for hidden rust on a used car?
qas.a: Yes. Rust detection includes: visual underbody inspection, checking door bottom edges (common rust point), wheel arch inner liners, boot floor, chassis rails, and floor pan. Surface rust is noted; structural rust is flagged as a serious issue.

qas.q: What is PDI (Pre-Delivery Inspection) for a new car?
qas.a: PDI is an independent inspection of a brand new car at the dealership before you take delivery. InspectCar's PDI covers 300+ checkpoints to ensure there is no transit damage, manufacturing defect, missing accessory, or documentation issue before you sign the delivery gate pass.

qas.q: Is PDI mandatory before taking delivery of a new car in India?
qas.a: PDI is not legally mandatory, but automotive experts and consumer protection advocates strongly recommend it for every new car buyer. InspectCar has found defects — including repainted panels, rat bite wiring, and wrong accessories — in over 25% of new cars inspected in Bangalore. Skipping PDI means accepting any pre-existing defect as your own problem post-delivery.

qas.q: How much does new car PDI cost in Bangalore?
qas.a: InspectCar's new car PDI (Pre-Drive package) costs ₹1,999 and covers 300+ checkpoints including paint gauge test, OBD scan, all electrical systems, documentation verification, and accessory check.

qas.q: How long does new car PDI take?
qas.a: InspectCar's new car PDI takes 45 to 75 minutes at the dealership or stockyard.

qas.q: When should I book a new car PDI?
qas.a: Book your PDI as soon as the dealer confirms a specific VIN/chassis number for your vehicle. Always book BEFORE the registration process begins. Once registered, you lose the leverage to demand defect rectification or a replacement vehicle.

qas.q: What happens if InspectCar finds defects during new car PDI?
qas.a: InspectCar's detailed PDF report with photos gives you documented evidence. qas.q: Can I reject a new car if PDI fails?
qas.a: Yes. Before signing the delivery gate pass and before registration, you have the right to refuse delivery or demand a defect-free replacement. InspectCar's inspection report provides the legal and moral basis for this demand.

qas.q: What does InspectCar check during new car PDI?
qas.a: InspectCar's 300+ point new car PDI covers: all body panels and paint (paint gauge test on every panel), all glass panes for OEM markings and chips, all electrical systems and infotainment, AC performance, OBD scan for pre-existing fault codes, all fluid levels, tyre condition and DOT code, underbody for transit damage, and complete documentation and accessory verification.

qas.q: Can a brand new car have paint defects from the factory?
qas.a: Yes. Factory paint defects include orange peel texture, paint runs, dirt inclusions, fish-eye marks, and uneven coverage. Transit handling can cause bumper or panel paint damage that dealers repair before delivery without disclosure. A paint gauge test detects all of these.

qas.q: What is stockyard damage in a new car?
qas.a: Stockyard damage occurs when cars are stored in dealer lots for weeks or months awaiting buyers. During this time, rats can chew wiring harnesses, battery voltage drops affecting ECU, UV exposure fades plastic trim, and hailstorms can cause small dents. InspectCar's PDI specifically inspects for all stockyard damage types.

qas.q: How can I tell if my new car was used as a demo car?
qas.a: Signs of a demo car include: odometer reading above 200 km, wear on driver's accelerator pedal rubber, scuffs on door sill entry plates, previous service history stamp in the service book, fuel level below full, and any interior wear not consistent with a brand new car.

qas.q: What documents should I check at new car delivery?
qas.a: Verify: Form 21 (Notice of dispatch from manufacturer), Form 22 (Roadworthiness certificate), manufacturer's invoice (check all accessories match), warranty booklet, owner's manual, insurance policy, 2 sets of keys, spare tyre with matching OEM size, wheel spanner and jack, and all accessories listed on your booking invoice.

qas.q: Does InspectCar check for rat bite wiring in new cars?
qas.a: Yes. Rat bite damage to wiring harnesses is a genuine problem in Bangalore dealership stockyards. Our PDI specifically inspects the engine bay wiring harness, underbody wiring, and runs a full electrical function test. If any electrical fault is found, we run an OBD scan to identify affected circuits.

qas.q: What is the OBD scan check in new car PDI?
qas.a: Even brand new cars can have pre-existing OBD fault codes from: factory calibration runs, transport handling, battery drain during storage, or ECU software issues. InspectCar runs a full OBD scan on every new car PDI. Any stored or pending DTCs are documented in the report so you can demand they be cleared and verified before taking delivery.

qas.q: Can InspectCar's PDI report help me get free accessories from the dealer?

qas.q: Is the price of a new car negotiable?
qas.a: New car ex-showroom prices are fixed, but on-road price components can be negotiated. Insurance premiums, extended warranty pricing, and accessories can be negotiated. InspectCar's PDI report, by documenting any defects, creates leverage to demand these value-additions at no extra cost.
